verdict: Mixing buys exactly one capability that no single paradigm has: a Graph can schedule a Swarm (or another Graph) as a node, so a deterministic state machine can contain one layer of autonomous handoffs. Swarm and the Workflow tool cannot host an orchestrator (probe). But on this linear research -> accounting -> writing task that capability adds no usable data power: E6 shows all three paradigms' structured state is trapped behind a text-only boundary, E7/E8 show an inner failure is either reported as success or is invisible to the Graph predicate, and the deliverable is identical across E1..E5. Meanwhile the cheapest pure run (E1 Graph) grows by 74.5% (E4) and 192.8% (E5) in tokens and up to 3.02x in wall clock. So: do NOT mix when the job is a linear chain and a downstream step must branch on a result. A pure Graph is both cheapest and the only layer that can still read its own nodes' status. Mix only when you specifically need one orchestrator nested inside a Graph AND you accept a text-only, non-auditable boundary.
tokens_note: E5 total = Graph's own accumulated_usage + inner Workflow task Agents' real accumulated_usage; the two are separate ledgers (E6/E7). E1/E3/E4 from result.accumulated_usage, E2 from per-task Agent usage.
